The image depicts two coffins and the word "NAIL."  This clearly points to the idiom related to death or the end of something.  Neither "nail down" (which means to finalize something) nor just "nail" alone fits.  While "nail in the coffin" is correct, "final nail in the coffin" or "last nail in the coffin" implies the ultimate action leading to an end, which makes more sense given the imagery.

The most appropriate answer here is either **(D) final nail in the coffin** or **(B) last nail in the coffin**.  These two phrases are often used interchangeably. If only one option can be selected, and there are two coffins, implying more than one nail has been driven, then (C) is the best answer.
